files.topic: Developmental timeline of fetal organ formation mapped to maternal nutrient demands
files.summary: Maps fetal organogenesis to nutrient-dependent windows: neural tube closure, placental iron prioritization, brain DHA accretion, fetal iron store building. Covers the biology behind why timing matters across phases.
files.when_to_reference: Phase transitions; explaining why a given nutrient is critical at a specific gestational age; biological-window rationale for measurement and supplementation cadence.

files.topic: Molecular mechanisms and bioavailable forms of pregnancy nutrients
files.summary: Per-nutrient biochemistry: pathway position, active vs inactive forms, bioavailability data, and why supplement form matters. Covers folate forms (methylfolate vs folic acid), B12 forms, iron forms (bisglycinate vs sulfate), vitamin D forms, vitamin A forms (retinol vs beta-carotene), magnesium forms.
files.when_to_reference: When evaluating supplement form preferences, explaining 'why this form over that form,' or interpreting why one product may underperform another at the same nominal dose.

files.topic: Lab markers and diagnostic interpretation in pregnancy with optimal-vs-standard ranges
files.summary: Marker-by-marker analysis of pregnancy lab interpretation: optimal vs standard reference ranges, evidence behind functional cutoffs, iron-panel interpretation matrix, B12 decision tree, ferritin acute-phase-reactant caveat, trimester-specific TSH ranges.
files.when_to_reference: Interpreting any lab result during pregnancy or lactation. Explaining why a value within standard 'normal' range may be inadequate for pregnancy. Building a recheck cadence.

files.topic: Genetic variants, dietary patterns, and pre-existing conditions affecting prenatal nutrition
files.summary: How individual variance modulates baseline nutrient status and supplementation response: MTHFR variants and folate metabolism, HFE variants and iron, vegan/vegetarian implications, comorbidity interactions (autoimmune thyroid, GDM risk, preeclampsia history).
files.when_to_reference: When the user has a known genetic variant, follows a restrictive diet, or has a pre-existing condition that may modulate prenatal supplementation needs.

files.topic: Supplement upper limits, teratogenicity, and dose-response in pregnancy
files.summary: Pregnancy-specific upper limits, teratogenicity mechanisms (vitamin A retinol), iron oxidative stress (Fenton chemistry), iodine narrow margin, vitamin D toxicity threshold, B6 neuropathy threshold, dose-response evidence per nutrient.
files.when_to_reference: When evaluating any supplement dose against safety, when the user asks 'is this too much,' when checking a product label against pregnancy ULs, when evaluating retinol-form vitamin A in skincare or supplements.

files.topic: Postpartum maternal recovery and lactation-phase nutrient supplementation
files.summary: Maternal depletion patterns by nutrient, Group I (diet-dependent) vs Group II (diet-independent) breast milk classification, lactation-specific dosing (vitamin D 6,400 IU evidence, EPA for postpartum mood), postpartum thyroiditis screening cadence, hemoglobin recovery timeline.
files.when_to_reference: Postpartum and lactation phases; explaining why lactation requires different vitamin D dosing than pregnancy; postpartum mood/mental-health connections to micronutrient status; recovery-timeline expectations after weaning.

files.topic: Evidence-quality assessment of prenatal nutrient research
files.summary: How to evaluate evidence quality across the prenatal-nutrition literature: RCT vs observational distinctions, supplement industry regulation context, third-party testing meaning and limits, product formulation gaps. Applies HC's multi-axis evidence framework to this domain.
files.when_to_reference: When the user asks 'how strong is the evidence on X,' when evaluating a supplement product claim, or when applying HC's epistemic-discipline rules to prenatal-specific research.
